title: Pouting Cat Emoji 😾 Meaning: Grumpy, Sulky, Not Amused
description: The 😾 pouting cat emoji is a scowling, sulking cat. It shows annoyance or a huff in a way that is hard to take too seriously. Meanings, examples and FAQs.
summary: The 😾 pouting cat emoji shows a cat with a deep frown and glaring eyes. It expresses annoyance, sulking, or grumpiness, usually over something minor. It is the cat counterpart of 😡, but its cuteness makes the anger look like a huff instead of real rage.
meaning: Anyone who has moved a sleeping cat off a chair knows this face. 😾 is displeasure with dignity: offended, sulking, and making sure you notice. People send it when plans change, when they are teased, when someone forgets to save them a seat. The complaint is real, but the delivery tells the other person it is safe to laugh and then apologize.

That gap between anger and cuteness is the reason to choose it over a red-faced smiley. A furious human face can escalate a disagreement. A cross cat keeps things affectionate, so couples and close friends use it to register a grievance without starting a fight. It is also used to describe someone else in a mood, or oneself before breakfast, in the same spirit as the internet's long love affair with grumpy-looking cats.

In pet posts the emoji is literal. It captions cats in sweaters, cats after baths, and cats whose dinner is four minutes late. Outside of that, it has no slang or hidden sense. One caution: at small sizes the slanted eyes can look like the smirking 😼, so a short message with only this emoji may leave the reader unsure whether you are cross or scheming.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Typical uses are mild protests: 'you ate my leftovers 😾' or 'still waiting on that reply 😾.' It asks for acknowledgment. Used toward a partner, it often means 'pay attention to me.' Answering with an apology or a peace offering emoji usually settles the matter.

contexts.label: On pet accounts
contexts.body: Owners post it with photos of unimpressed cats: ears back, eyes narrowed, tail flicking. The joke is the cat's apparent sense of injustice over a costume, a new kitten, or a closed door. Followers reply with it to voice the cat's opinion on its behalf.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: People use 😾 to grumble about everyday irritations such as Monday mornings, delayed trains, or a favorite show being canceled. It signals irritation while keeping the post lighthearted. Fans also use it in mock protest when an artist delays a release.

examples.text: You started the new season without me 😾
examples.meaning: A sulky complaint that invites an apology.

examples.text: Alarm went off at 5am for no reason 😾
examples.meaning: General grumpiness about a bad start to the day.

examples.text: Bath time went about as well as expected 😾🛁
examples.meaning: A pet owner describing a very unhappy cat.
The sender is clearly not fine and is in a huff.

combos.meaning: Properly irritated, with the anger mark turning up the heat.
From sulking to forgiving, used when making up.

confusedWith.difference: 😡 is a red, furious human face that reads as serious anger. 😾 expresses the same feeling at a lower temperature and with humor, so it is better for small annoyances and affectionate sulking.
😼 has similar slanted eyes but a mouth that curls into a smirk, signaling smugness. 😾 has a downturned mouth and means displeasure. They are easy to confuse at a glance.
😿 is sad, with a tear, and asks for comfort. 😾 is annoyed and asks for an apology. Choose based on whether you feel hurt or cross.

avoid: Do not use it when you are truly upset and need to be taken seriously, because the cute cat will soften your message too much.
Avoid sending it to a manager or client to complain, where sulking reads as unprofessional.
design: A cat's head with ears and whiskers, eyes or brows slanted sharply inward, and a mouth pulled down into a frown or tight pout. Fur is yellow or orange on most platforms. Some vendors add furrowed brows or puffed cheeks. The overall impression ranges from sulky to stern depending on the design.

faqs.q: What does 😾 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: She is annoyed or sulking, usually playfully. It often means she wants attention, an apology, or for you to notice something you missed. If the rest of the message is short and cold, take the annoyance more seriously.

faqs.q: What does 😾 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: He is grumpy or pretending to be offended. It is a soft way to complain without sounding aggressive. Between partners, it tends to be affectionate pouting.
Angry, in a mild and sulky way. 'Pouting' here follows the older sense of a displeased expression. For sadness, the crying cat 😿 is the right choice.

faqs.q: What is the human version of 😾?
faqs.a: It corresponds to 😡, which Unicode originally named Pouting Face. The cat was designed as its counterpart when both were standardized in 2010.
